title: Algorithms for Quantum Computation: Discrete Logarithms and Factoring
venue: IEEE FOCS (35th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science)
abstract: A digital computer running quantum algorithms can factor integers and find discrete logarithms in polynomial time O((log N)^3), breaking RSA and Diffie-Hellman cryptosystems.
fullExcerpt: Quantum computers can solve prime factorization in polynomial time by finding the period of modular exponentiation using the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT). Classical factoring requires sub-exponential time via the Number Field Sieve.

precomputedClaims.claim: Shor's algorithm achieves polynomial time factoring O((log N)^3).
precomputedClaims.sourceQuote: A quantum computer can factor integers in polynomial time.
precomputedClaims.notes: Relies on Quantum Fourier Transform for phase estimation.

openGaps: Requires thousands of logical qubits with fault-tolerant surface codes to factor 2048-bit RSA.
